blocks.text: # Cross-fixture Artifact Binding Replication Plan
## Purpose and claim boundary

This is a preregistered **APEX-derived Artifact Handoff Track**, not an
official APEX score and not a general claim that Proofpress improves agent
task performance. It follows the repaired local-debug SPA finding: a native
Proofpress package detected a stale DOCX semantic binding that an
information-matched ordinary handoff did not detect.

The replication asks a narrower question: across independently authored
artifact families and fault mechanisms, does the C2 portable accepted-history
package reduce unsafe continuation relative to the same C1 ordinary handoff,
without an unacceptable clean-admission or operational cost?
## Treatment and isolation

The primary contrast is C2 minus C1. C1 and C2 receive byte-identical current
artifact(s), task, natural handoff, tools, model configuration, token cap, and
schedule. C2 alone adds the native Proofpress carrier, accepted head,
decision/evidence links, artifact binding, semantic evidence where supported,
and a package-local verification tool. C0 is retained as a contextual
artifact-only control; it is not the primary product comparison.

Each receiver workspace is fresh. A host-side, local-only Git object store is
provisioned before C2 starts; the agent may invoke the package-local verifier
but may not create a repository, access a remote, or inspect host state.
Every C2 cell records verifier-preflight telemetry. A missing or failed
preflight invalidates that attempt regardless of disposition.
## Fixture and threat matrix

Phase R1 has four independent fixture families. They are built and qualified
before any paid execution; no planned fixture is evidence until its immutable
case manifest and Phase 0 report pass.

| Fixture family | Native artifact | Clean state | Fault state | Mechanism under test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 legal agreement | DOCX | current accepted agreement | semantic stale binding with matching coarse structure | semantic DOCX evidence detects an unrecorded material edit |
| F2 operating policy | Markdown plus exported PDF | current approved policy | superseded accepted head | accepted-history lineage distinguishes current from valid old content |
| F3 technical specification | Markdown or DOCX | current implementation specification | wrong artifact binding | binding connects the accepted decision trail to the selected deliverable |
| F4 decision revision | DOCX | current revision after a rejected alternative | revived rejected branch | recorded rejection prevents a plausible but unauthorized continuation |

The fault must be plausible under C1's ordinary handoff and must not expose an
arm label, oracle, fault label, expected disposition, or a rubric-answer
summary. C1 may be useful and professionally realistic, but it may not embed
hashes, a version graph, decision status inventory, or verifier output.
## Endpoints, analysis, and gates

Primary endpoint: paired C2 minus C1 unsafe-proceed rate on fault cells.
Co-primary guardrail: C2 clean correct-admission rate, reported with a
predeclared non-inferiority margin of 10 percentage points. Do not collapse
safety and clean admission into one utility score.

Secondary outcomes are correct safe disposition, verifier-process completion,
time, cost, tool turns, and—for clean continuation cells only—native
task-quality completion. Fault cells have no downstream-artifact denominator.

R1 uses three independently randomized receiver repeats per arm, state, and
fixture: 4 fixtures times 3 arms times 2 states times 3 repeats equals 72
eligible receiver cells. Each fixture is analyzed first; a pooled estimate is
reported only with fixture-stratified effects and never substitutes for them.

Advance to an external or more realistic benchmark replication only if all
four fixture Phase 0 gates pass, all production cells have complete telemetry,
no fixture has a C2 unsafe continuation attributable to a carrier or binding
fault, the pooled C2-C1 safety effect is favorable, and the lower bound of the
clean-admission difference exceeds minus 10 points. A null, heterogeneous, or
clean-path-regressive result stops expansion and is retained as evidence.
## Execution sequence
1. Author each fixture independently, freeze artifact, handoff, scorer, and
hidden oracle hashes, then run no-model Phase 0.
2. Run a blinded package audit for C1/C2 parity, leakage, real carrier
import/verify, binding-fault detection, and scoreability.
3. Run a 12-cell qualification slice: C1/C2 by clean/fault across the first
three fixture families. Do not pool with the prior SPA local-debug result.
4. If the predeclared qualification gates pass, execute R1 under a fresh API

key, bare mode, and actual OS sandbox; preserve every failed attempt and
   replace only infrastructure-invalid cells under the frozen retry rule.
5. Publish the bounded, fixture-stratified result and decide whether an
external benchmark replication is justified.
## Current status

This plan is design-only. The repaired SPA local-debug cohort is a mechanism
calibration supporting F1's threat model; it neither satisfies R1 nor grants
permission to claim cross-fixture efficacy. The next implementation deliverable
is a fixture registry and deterministic validator that prevents launch until
all required package and oracle fields are frozen.
